messages.subject: calender_date and L5hr_ENMO_mg_0-24hr
parts:
Hi everyone, 

Apologies if this is a bit of a silly question - I'm just having trouble getting my head around one output from GGIR. 

I'm currently trying to look at an analysis where we want to investigate the relationship between circadian rhythm disturbance, particularly delays in L5 onset and pain and fatigue in patients with a form of arthritis.

We have collected daily symptom questionnaires for 28 days (completed in the AM upon waking up) and have ~25 complete nights of GENEActiv actigraphy which we've run through GGIR. 

From our part2_daysummary, we want to look at the previous night's L5hr_ENMO_mg_0-24hr and then explore against the symptom questionnaire completed the next morning. Would we take say the L5hr from 01/02/2022 and pair this with the questionnaire from 02/02/2022 or is the ENMO readout on from calendar_date 02/02/2022 corresponding to the previous nights L5 onset? 

Many thanks in advance 
Dylan

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] calender_date and L5hr_ENMO_mg_0-24hr
parts:
L5hr_ENMO_mg_0-24hr is not night specific but specific to the 24 hour window between midnights. Input argument dayborder allows you to modify the location start/end of the 24 hour day and by that effectively change the definition of midnight. This should be used with caution as it will also affect all other GGIR output because it fundamentally changes the definition of a day.

Vincent
